To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
racial/ethnic minority youth who have sex with males are not accessing health care and are not being prescribed antiretrovirus therapy, despite being HIV positive.
racial/ethnic minority youth have lower CD4 cell counts and higher viral loads than non-Hispanic white youth, and the use of ART is associated with lower viral loads.

among racial/ ethnic minority YMSM who are HIV infected, the baseline CD4 count is influenced by age, drug and alcohol usage, mental health symptoms, and ART usage, while viral load is influenced by age and ART usage.

the development of an intervention to increase the proportion of racial/ethnic minority HIV-positive YMSM who are engaged in medical care and who are taking ART.
the health care utilization patterns of HIV-positive racial/ethnic minority youth.
the health care utilization, health status and outcomes, and risk behaviors of a cohort of racial/ethnic minority HIV-infected YMSM.

the study findings indicate that the majority of the cohort had detectable viral loads and were not prescribed ART.
the current study found that among racial/ ethnic minority YMSM with a CD4 count ≤ 350 cells/mL, only one-half of this cohort was prescribed ART to treat the infection.
racial/ethnic minority HIV-infected YMSM are not being engaged in medical care and are not receiving the benefits of ART.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the HRSA-funded outreach, linkage, retention, and reengagement program is effective for increasing the use of ART and achieving HIV suppression in racial/ethnic minority HIV-infected YMSM.
the majority of HIV-positive minority YMSM were not on ART, but of those that were started on ART the majority did achieve undetectably low viral loads.
we have identified the need to provide more comprehensive services for HIV-infected racial and ethnic minority youth.

the majority of HIV-positive YMSM who are on ART have undetectable viral load.
